title: RoleSet ownership & scope isolation: RBAC v2 model and permission matrix
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design ticket for the RBAC v2 role model focusing on RoleSets, resource ownership, scope isolation, and a permissions matrix that maps to audit logs and SSO/SAML role mappings. Outcome: a canonical model and migration-ready spec for implementing RoleSets + hierarchical resource scoping across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes.
decisions: Adopt RoleSet abstraction (collection of permissions + metadata) rather than flat roles to enable composition and inheritance across tenants and teams.
Resource scoping will be hierarchical: Organization > Project > Deployment > Resource (model/route/instance). Permissions evaluate at the narrowest matching scope with explicit deny precedence.
Scopes are first-class strings with namespace format (org:team:project:resource). We'll support wildcard scoping for legacy mappings but discourage it in UI and recommend least privilege defaults.
Audit logs will record evaluated RoleSet, resolved effective permissions, scope match path, SAML/SSO assertion id, and policy version for every admin-level action.
SSO/SAML role mapping will map IdP group claims to RoleSets and to temporary session attributes; group-to-roleset mapping will be editable per-organization in Console.
Migration path: existing RBAC v1 roles will be converted to read-only RoleSets and admins will be given a "v1 compatibility" RoleSet for 90 days before manual reconciliation.
Deny entries override allow entries in evaluation to handle emergency access revocation and cross-tenant safety.
Owner tag on resources will be enforced; owners get an implicit ResourceOwner RoleSet scope for their owned resource only (no org-wide privileges unless explicitly granted).
tradeoffs: RoleSet composition increases flexibility but adds complexity to UI; we will provide opinionated defaults and a guided 'Create RoleSet' flow.

Recording full evaluation details in audit logs improves post-incident forensics but increases log volume and storage cost; we will sample non-admin operations and store full traces for admin-level events only by default.
Wildcard scopes ease migration but reduce visibility into least-privilege; we'll support migration helpers to progressively tighten scopes.
Immediate deny precedence simplifies revocation semantics but requires careful test coverage to avoid accidental lockouts; provide a built-in escape hatch for org admins under support.
SSO group syncing latency can cause short-lived permission gaps; we will issue a short-lived session refresh instruction in the Console when mapping changes occur.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical RoleSet schema documented in Confluence with examples for Org, Project, Deployment, and Resource-level scopes.
Permission evaluation algorithm implemented in the auth service with unit tests covering precedence, inheritance, and wildcard cases.
Audit log schema updated to include roleset_id, effective_permissions, scope_match_path, saml_assertion_id, and policy_version. Backfill test in staging shows correct entries for sample actions.
Console UI mock for RoleSet creation and SSO group mapping reviewed and approved by Design and PM.
Migration script to convert RBAC v1 roles to RoleSets is available and tested on a staging tenant with no regressions.
Performance test: permission evaluation latency p50 <= 2ms, p99 <= 8ms under typical load; auth cache miss handled within 25ms.
Security review completed and signed off by Security team.
E2E tests show SSO group -> RoleSet mapping applied during login and audit entry created for a sample admin action.
migration_plan: Phase 0 (Design): finalize RoleSet schema and eval algorithm. Owners: Miguel + Asha. ETA 2025-02-18.
Phase 1 (Infra): implement extended audit schema and auth API endpoints for RoleSets. Feature flag behind 'rbac_v2'. ETA 2025-02-28.

Phase 2 (Migration tooling): create automated converter that maps RBAC v1 roles to RoleSets and emits a reconciliation report. Run on staging tenants; get approval from two pilot customers. ETA 2025-03-07.
Phase 3 (Console + SSO): UI for RoleSet management and IdP mapping. Provide 'compatibility mode' toggle in org settings. ETA 2025-03-15.

Phase 4 (Rollout): opt-in pilot for a subset of customers, monitor audit logs for missing privileges, iterate mapping helpers. Full rollout gated on performance and security signoff. ETA target 2025-04-01.
Rollback: revert to RBAC v1 RoleSet compatibility flag; maintain legacy token validation for 90 days following flip.
rollout_steps: Create feature flag 'rbac_v2' and release auth changes behind flag.
Deploy audit schema change with backward-compatible fields and run migration to populate roleset_id for new events.
Run converter on test orgs and generate reconciliation reports for org admins.
Enable Console RoleSet UI for internal pilot orgs and gather feedback.
Open pilot to selected customers and monitor customer_impact signals and SLOs.
Gradually flip default to RBAC v2 for new orgs; provide in-console wizard for existing orgs to migrate.
After 90 days and no critical issues, retire RBAC v1 read-only compatibility layer.
tests: Unit tests for evaluator covering: exact scope match, ancestor scope match, wildcard scope expansion, explicit deny precedence, owner implicit grant.
Integration tests: login flow with SAML group mapping -> session contains roleset ids; API call shows expected permission set and audit record.
Load tests: auth service under 10k req/s with realistic cache hit ratios; ensure p99 eval latency <= 10ms.
Chaos test: revoke a RoleSet deny entry and validate immediate effect across multiple service instances.
Migration dry-run test: run converter on staging and verify reconciliation report matches manual mapping for sample orgs.
